arxiv-2202-12980.title: Simulability of high-dimensional quantum measurements
arxiv-2202-12980.creator: Marie Ioannou, Pavel Sekatski, Sébastien Designolle, Benjamin D.M. Jones, Roope Uola, Nicolas Brunner
arxiv-2202-12980.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marie Ioannou, Pavel Sekatski, Sébastien Designolle, Benjamin D.M. Jones, Roope Uola, Nicolas Brunner. We investigate the compression of quantum information with respect to a given set ℳ \mathcal{M} of high-dimensional measurements. This leads to a notion of simulability, where we demand that the statistics obtained from ℳ \mathcal{M} and an arbitrary quantum state ρ \rho are recovered exactly by first compressing ρ \rho into a lower dimensional space, followed by some quantum measurements.

arxiv-2310-14807.title: On Chaitin’s Heuristic Principle and Halting Probability
arxiv-2310-14807.creator: Saeed Salehi Research Center of Biosciences & Biotechnology (RCBB), University of Tabriz, P.O.Box 51666–16471, Tabriz, IRAN. E-mail: root@SaeedSalehi.ir
arxiv-2310-14807.description: Abstract It would be a heavenly reward if there were a method of weighing theories and sentences in such a way that a theory could never prove a heavier sentence (Chaitin’s Heuristic Principle). Alas, no satisfactory measure has been found so far, and this dream seemed too good to ever come true.

arxiv-2406-19356.title: DiVERT: Di stractor Generation with V ariational E rrors R epresented as T ext for Math Multiple-choice Questions
arxiv-2406-19356.creator: Nigel Fernandez, Alexander Scarlatos, Wanyong Feng, Simon Woodhead, Andrew Lan
arxiv-2406-19356.description: Abstract High-quality distractors are crucial to both the assessment and pedagogical value of multiple-choice questions (MCQs), where manually crafting ones that anticipate knowledge deficiencies or misconceptions among real students is difficult. Meanwhile, automated distractor generation, even with the help of large language models (LLMs), remains challenging for subjects like math.

arxiv-2502-14798.title: Unlocking the Optoelectronic Potential of AGeX 3 (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = S, Se): A Sustainable Alternative in Chalcogenide Perovskites
arxiv-2502-14798.creator: Ayan Chakravorty, Surajit Adhikari ∗ , and Priya Johari
arxiv-2502-14798.description: Abstract The quest for environmentally benign and stable optoelectronic materials has intensified, and chalcogenide perovskites (CPs) have emerged as promising candidates owing to their non-toxic composition, stability, small bandgaps, large absorption coefficients. However, a detailed theoretical study of excitonic and polaronic properties of these materials remains underexplored due to high computational demands.

arxiv-2508-05163.title: Preparing for the worst: Long-term and short-term weather extremes in resource adequacy assessment
arxiv-2508-05163.creator: Aleksander Grochowicz, Hannah C. Bloomfield, Marta Victoria
arxiv-2508-05163.description: Abstract Abstract Security of supply is a common and important concern when integrating renewables in net-zero power systems. Extreme weather affects both demand and supply leading to power system stress; in Europe this stress spreads continentally beyond the meteorological root cause.

arxiv-2510-18953.title: The B + → K + ​ ν ​ ν ¯ B^{+}\to K^{+}\nu\bar{\nu} decay as a search for the QCD axion
arxiv-2510-18953.creator: Merna Abumusabh, Giulio Dujany, Diego Guadagnoli, Axel Iohner, Claudio Toni
arxiv-2510-18953.description: Abstract We reinterpret the B + → K + ​ ν ​ ν ¯ B^{+}\to K^{+}\nu\bar{\nu} measurement as a probe of the decay B + → K + ​ a B^{+}\to K^{+}a , where a a denotes an axion or axion-like particle.

europmc-pmc8106911.creator: Hockenberry AJ, Wilke CO.
europmc-pmc8106911.description: Bacteriophages are broadly classified into two distinct lifestyles: temperate and virulent. pmc-10571034.title: Tobacco toxins induce osteoporosis through ferroptosis
pmc-10571034.creator: Zheng Jing, Yuzhou Li, He Zhang, Tao Chen, Jinrui Yu, Xinxin Xu, Yulong Zou, Xu Wang, Kai Xiang, Xuerui Gong, Ping He, Yiru Fu, Mingxing Ren, Ping Ji, Sheng Yang
pmc-10571034.description: Clinical epidemiological studies have confirmed that tobacco smoking disrupts bone homeostasis and is an independent risk factor for the development of osteoporosis. The low viability and inferior osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are important etiologies of osteoporosis.

pmc-11413533.title: Phenotypic age mediates effects of Life's Essential 8 on reduced mortality risk in US adults
pmc-11413533.creator: Yuxuan Zhao, Haiming Yang, Rong Jiao, Yueqing Wang, Meng Xiao, Mingyu Song, Huan Yu, Chunxiao Liao, Yuanjie Pang, Wenjing Gao, Tao Huang, Canqing Yu, Jun Lv, Shengxu Li, Lu Qi, Liming Li, Dianjianyi Sun
pmc-11413533.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to find out whether phenotypic age could mediate the protective effects of a healthy lifestyle on mortality.MethodsWe included adult participants with available data for individual phenotypic age (PhenoAge) and Life's Essential 8 (LE8) scores from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005–2010 (three cycles) and linked mortality records until 31 December 2019.

pmc-11678114.title: Bioinformatic Tools for Studying the Cellular Immune Response to SARS-CoV-2, Vaccine Efficacy, and Future Pandemics at the Global Population Level
pmc-11678114.creator: Daniel López, Javier Zumárraga, Zhifang Zhang
pmc-11678114.description: Antigen recognition by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) restriction is critical for an adequate antiviral response in both natural infection and vaccination. However, the overwhelming polymorphism of HLA, with nearly 40,000 alleles identified, is an important limitation for the global analysis of cellular immune responses and vaccine efficacy.

pmc-11861437.title: A tale of two belongings: social and academic belonging differentially shape academic and psychological outcomes among university students
pmc-11861437.creator: Smaranda Ioana Lawrie, Delwin B. Carter, Karen Nylund-Gibson, Heejung S. Kim
pmc-11861437.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The benefits of belonging in academic settings are well established; however, past empirical research has for the most part conflated academic and social belonging. This study utilized latent class analysis (LCA) with a sample of undergraduates (N = 837) to determine whether distinct classes or profiles of belonging exist on a college campus and whether class membership predicts academic and psychological outcomes.

pmc-12700908.title: Upper limb function and quality of life in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a cross-sectional study in Chile
pmc-12700908.creator: Daniela Avila-Smirnow, Carla Pérez, Odalie Moscoso, Nayadeth Lucero-González
pmc-12700908.description: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) impairs motor function and health-related quality of life (HRQoL), yet data from low- and middle-income countries are scarce. We assessed upper limb functionality with the Upper Limb Functionality Evaluation Scale (EEFES) and HRQoL with the SF36v2 in Chilean patients with DMD at late ambulatory and nonambulatory stages, comparing them with healthy age-matched controls.

pmc-12788575.title: Development, Validity, and Test Reliability and Reproducibility of Facial Palsy-Associated Facial Movement: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12788575.creator: Devang Deshpande, Kumar Chowdary Yaramati, Charan Teja Bobba, Meena Priya, Sai Charan Pasupuleti, Sajan Anand Gubbala, Nandisha Thakkar
pmc-12788575.description: Background:Facial palsy impairs facial muscle function, impacting both physical and psychosocial well-being. Existing assessment tools often lack sensitivity or functional comprehensiveness. This study aimed to develop and validate a novel facial palsy functional assessment scale (FPFAS) to address these limitations.Methods:A cross-sectional study was conducted in two phases.

pmc-12973863.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation mitigates perioperative neurocognitive disorders by regulating the function of the glymphatic system
pmc-12973863.creator: Xuanran Feng, Jiehui Liu, Zhanping Liang, Xue Du, Lijuan Zhao, Ning Xie, Changqi Chen, Lu Ding, Xiaohuan Xia, Jialin C. Zheng, Jianhui Liu
pmc-12973863.description: The incidence of perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) increase with age, especially within those countries facing great challenge of aging population. However, the mechanism of PND remains elusive, and the lack of precautions has resulted in extended recovery among the elderly. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has shown promising therapeutic potential in many neurological disorders such as depression and Alzheimer’s disease.

pmc-13030828.title: Competition in the Segregation Mechanism of Granular Flow Within a 2D Rotating Drum Based on Magnetic Positioning Technology
pmc-13030828.creator: Rong Pan, Zhi-Peng Chi, Yi-Ming Li, Ran Li, Hui Yang
pmc-13030828.description: Accurate monitoring of internal particle motion in dense granular flows remains a significant challenge across various fields, ranging from geophysics to industrial processes. To address the limitations of existing observational techniques, this study presents a novel high-precision magnetic array positioning system based on magnetic dipole theory for dynamically tracking individual particles within opaque granular media.

pmc-13105892.title: Case Report: Successful endoscopic resection of a huge rectal tumor extending to the dentate line and associated with a diverticulum by endoscopic submucosal dissection
pmc-13105892.creator: Bing-Jie Yan, Yu-Fan Li, Ze Qi, Ming-Wei Zhang, Lei Li
pmc-13105892.description: BackgroundRectal tumors extending to the dentate line (RTDL) represent a distinct subtype of rectal neoplasms due to the unique anatomical features of the dentate line, for which endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has proven to be an effective therapeutic approach. Furthermore, when tumors invade diverticula, the likelihood of perforation during ESD markedly escalates.

pmc-13205295.title: A First-Principles Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation for Shortcuts to Adiabaticity
pmc-13205295.creator: Guillermo Ezequiel Perna, Federico Centrone, Esteban Calzetta
pmc-13205295.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We study the fundamental limitations of implementing time-dependent Hamiltonian protocols when “time” is provided by a quantum clock rather than an external classical parameter. For a parametric harmonic oscillator controlled through a shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) schedule and coupled to a minimal clock degree of freedom, tracing out the clock yields an effective reduced dynamics that is a mixture of unitary Gaussian trajectories.

pmc-13408337.title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered fecal metabolome in patients with age-related cataract
pmc-13408337.creator: Yingying Liu, Cun Sun, Hongyu Liu, Xinjie Shu, Ting Yu, Yu Gong, Jiawen Li
pmc-13408337.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Age-related cataract (ARC) is a leading cause of vision loss with incompletely understood mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests the gut microbiota can influence ocular health, yet the gut–eye connection in cataract remains unexplored. We characterized gut microbial communities and fecal metabolic profiles in 30 ARC patients and 30 healthy controls using 16S rDNA gene sequencing, untargeted LC–MS metabolomics, and targeted GC–MS for short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs).

pmc-13584503.title: Association of the atherogenic index of plasma and its integrative novel adiposity-based composites with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: novel adiposity-derived AIP indices provide modest incremental prognostic information
pmc-13584503.creator: Sheng Wei, Jiajun Qiu, Yong Liu, Ning Xu, Zhonghua Sun, Sha Li, Changping He, Xiangping Xie, Yanlang He
pmc-13584503.description: BackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is recognized as a progressive pathophysiological continuum linking metabolic dysfunction, dysfunctional adiposity, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular injury. The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) reflects lipid-related atherogenic burden, whereas novel adiposity indices, including body roundness index (BRI), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and a body shape index (ABSI), capture body-shape-related adiposity burden.

pmc-13643554.title: First Report of Antegrade Transeptal Valve-in-Valve TAVR
pmc-13643554.creator: Jeffrey Rossi, Robert Hoffberger, Thomas P. Archer, David C. Buck, Michael Mollod, Daniel Molloy, Jonathan Hoffberger, Jeffrey Sell
pmc-13643554.description: ObjectiveTo outline the procedural steps for a transfemoral, antegrade valve in a transcatheter aortic valve replacement procedure in a patient with no other access options.Key StepsGain femoral venous and arterial access. Position a snare in the ascending aorta. Perform transseptal puncture. From the left atrium, deliver an 0.035-inch wire through the mitral valve and aortic valve into the ascending aorta.

pmc-13688458.title: Clinical Trial of Tolvaptan in Pediatric ADPKD: Two-Year, Open-Label Extension
pmc-13688458.creator: Djalila Mekahli, Lisa M Guay-Woodford, Melissa A Cadnapaphornchai, Larry A Greenbaum, Mieczyslaw Litwin, Tomas Seeman, Ann Dandurand, Zhen Zhang, Kimberly Sikes, Susan E Shoaf, Franz Schaefer, Pediatric Trial Investigators
pmc-13688458.description: IntroductionTolvaptan is indicated for adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) at increased risk of rapid progression. Pharmacodynamic activity and acceptable safety and tolerability were demonstrated in a 1-year, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in children and adolescents with ADPKD (Phase A of a 2-part, phase-3b study [NCT02964273]). Here, the 2-year, open-label extension (Phase B) is reported.
